*Updated 2026-10-04 · 112 works indexed · regenerated after each daily run.*

One hundred and twelve works. The October 4 piece scores 2, bringing the last twelve to 1, 2, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 1, 1, 2 — median 2, with the two 3s still the ceiling and no 4 since late July. That is now fourteen weeks without a 4. The pattern is stable in the wrong direction.

Camera position has not moved. Straight-on sits at 27 of 112 all-time, overhead at 11, from-behind at 10, low-angle at 4. The last twelve show no overhead, no low-angle, and no through-frame — the same convergence flagged for three consecutive memos. The September 7 hoofprint piece and the September 25 barometer piece each scored 3 by achieving perceptual estrangement through scale rather than axis displacement, which confirms that estrangement is the operative variable, not any specific technique. But scale violation itself has thinned to 4 of the last 12 against 30 of 112 all-time, and the two recent 3s exhausted the same mechanism twice in a row. A third consecutive scale-as-estrangement approach will produce another 2. The displacement needs to come from somewhere the camera hasn't been in over a month: directly overhead, or low enough that the focal object becomes ceiling.

Figure count remains at none or one across the full recent window. The archive's 4-scored works all depended on something going wrong between bodies — the wrong number, the wrong posture, the wrong gaze — which a single figure or no figure structurally cannot produce. A second figure placed incorrectly still outperforms any second accident on a figureless frame. The October 4 piece uses zero figures and scores 2; the barbed wire fence is doing the work a body should be doing.

Three registers remain dormant: reprieve once in 112 works, reckoning twice, encroachment once. They should return only when the specific anchor makes them unavoidable. Aftermath and menace together account for 44 of 112 all-time and continue to dominate the recent window, which is not yet a problem but is approaching one.

Fourteen weeks of median 2 is not a plateau — it is a floor that has been mistaken for ground. Move the camera axis or introduce a second figure doing something wrong, and do it before the next piece, not as a general intention.
